name: Cowrie Shell Currency
region: Global (China, India, West Africa, Oceania, Southeast Asia)
summary: Natural shell-based monetary system that functioned as standardised currency across three continents for over 3000 years, requiring no central mint and resisting counterfeiting.

claims.statement: Cowrie shells served as currency in Shang Dynasty China (c. 1200 BCE) and remained legal tender in parts of West Africa into the 20th century
The system required no centralised minting authority — shells were naturally standardised, portable, durable, and difficult to counterfeit
Cowrie networks connected Indian Ocean, West African, and East Asian trade systems independently of European monetary frameworks

evidence.source: Peng (2000) A Monetary History of China, Western Washington University
Hogendorn & Johnson (1986) The Shell Money of the Slave Trade, Cambridge UP
Yang (2011) A Commodity-Money Theory of Cowrie Shells in Ancient China, Economic History Review 64(2)
Maldivian cowrie shell export sites, dating 1st millennium CE, documented by Heimann (1980)
Pallaver (2009) A Recognized Currency in Beads: Glass Beads as Money in 19th-Century East Africa, Africa 79(3)

notes: Maximum decentralisation: no mint, no state backing, no forgery problem. Demonstrates that robust monetary systems can emerge without central authority — the I/O system can self-organise.
